details: CONFIRMED with bun RegExp over JSON.stringify({command, description}): false for the env-prefixed command, true for
"openspec list". The anchor allows only ^{"command":", ; & | ( or \n before the program, so VAR=value openspec ... and
env openspec ... slip through. A max-0 grader that misses a real form is a hidden regression path. Size: 10.
failing_case: Bash input {"command":"OPENSPEC_TELEMETRY=0 openspec validate sort-by-name --strict"} (this exact form is in the surviving
traces /private/tmp/e-iZGYAB and e-oM3l1E) does not match the new pattern: the grader stays quiet although an openspec
command ran. Expected: it matches (max 0 fails the run). Same for the two other no-spec-step* copies.
fix_hint: Allow optional VAR=value words (and env) before the program: ...\s*(?:[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*=\S*\s+)*(?:(?:env|npx|bunx)\s+)?openspec\s+[a-z]
in all three copies, and add the case to the test.
pass_cases: 1. "OPENSPEC_TELEMETRY=0 openspec validate x --strict" -> match.
2. "openspec new change sort-by-name", "cd .worktrees/x && openspec validate x", "ls; openspec list", "npx openspec init" -> match (as now).
3. "find .claude openspec docs -type f | head -40", "ls openspec/changes", "git add openspec && git commit -m x" -> no match (as now).
4. tests/test_wave_red.py carries case 1, checked with bun RegExp (the grader's dialect).
reason: tests/test_wave_red.py NoOpenspecCommand::test_running_the_openspec_program_is_caught passes, fails with the old grader.
findings.summary: the new no-openspec-command pattern misses an openspec command behind an env prefix, a form sessions really use

details: CONFIRMED by reading the prompt against the grader text. A grader that the prompt itself satisfies measures instruction
following, not the rule ("a test that passes with the behaviour disabled"). The remaining relay-term-defined failures
(04-17-00, 04-39-18) are then judge noise on an instruction, not evidence about the rule. Size: 15 plus a paid proof.
evidence: git diff master...HEAD -- evals/plugin/it-terms-ru/prompt.md (new text quoted above);
evals/plugin/it-terms-ru/graders/relay-term-defined: "give a one-line definition of it the first time it appears".
failing_case: The prompt now says "Полный локальный прогон проверок перед слиянием в проекте называют gate ... В этот прогон входят тесты,
линтер и проверка типов ... объясни одной фразой, что такое gate". The grader relay-term-defined asks whether the reply
defines "gate" at first use, which the rule "a relay-specific term gets its English name and a one-line definition the
first time" requires. A session with no rule at all, told to define gate and given the definition, passes it.
Expected: the prompt names the term without asking for its definition, so a pass shows the rule at work.
fix_hint: Keep "read CLAUDE.md" and "the gate passed"; drop the list of what gate runs and the request to explain it.
pass_cases: 1. The it-terms-ru prompt names gate (and that it passed) but does not ask "what is gate" nor list what it runs.
2. A recorded reply that uses "gate" with no definition is judged FAIL by relay-term-defined (judge-measure item).
3. it-terms-ru still sends the session to read CLAUDE.md (the set-up fix stays).
reason: tests/test_wave_red.py ItTermsPromptsDoNotGiveTheAnswer::test_ru_prompt_names_gate_without_defining_or_asking_for_it passes, fails with the old prompt.
findings.summary: the it-terms-ru prompt now hands over the gate definition and asks for it, so relay-term-defined passes with the rule absent

details: CONFIRMED by reading. This text loads into the CLAUDE.md of every synced project. The sentence is shaped on the
it-terms graders (english-terms-kept wants merge, branch, fast-forward, hook), and the word list "страховка", "gancho"

evidence: git diff master...HEAD -- rules/working-with-me.md; report: "(this alone did not change the result; kept because it is the
failing_case: Owner (Russian) asks "что с веткой, её слили?" about a plain merge where no hook fired. The new line "A reply that explains
a merge names merge, branch and hook (and fast-forward, ...) in English" tells the model to bring up a hook that played
no part. Expected: the rule says to keep the terms in English when they are used, not which terms a merge reply contains.
fix_hint: Keep the "even when my own message uses the local word" sentence (with general examples, ветка/слияние, rama/fusión);
drop "A reply that explains a merge names merge, branch and hook ...".
pass_cases: 1. rules/working-with-me.md keeps "Standard IT terms stay in their English form", "one-line definition the first time" and

2. The rule keeps the point that a local word in the owner's message is still written as the English term.
3. No sentence of the rule prescribes which terms a reply about a merge must contain.
reason: tests/test_wave_red.py ItTermsPromptsDoNotGiveTheAnswer::test_rule_does_not_prescribe_the_terms_of_a_merge_reply passes, fails with the old rule.
findings.summary: the synced rule now tells every session that any merge explanation names a hook, and lists the eval prompt's own words
